We applied template 1209837 (retro smarts: [C:3]-[C:2](-[C:4])-[OH;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(=C)-C(=O)-[O;H0;D2;+0:1]-[C:2](-[C:3])-[C:4]) to our target. The result is a precursor: "C=C(C)C(=O)O[C@@]1(C(F)(F)F)CCC[C@H]1C(=C)c1ccccc1". Let's verify if this matches the expected transformation: The target has a carbonyl-ene reaction product; retrosynthesis should break to a ketone and alkene. The precursor we got is a molecule with a carbonyl (C=O) and an alkene? It has C=C(C)C(=O)O... Actually the SMILES: C=C(C)C(=O)O[C@@]1(C(F)(F)F)CCC[C@H]1C(=C)c1ccccc1. This looks like a cyclohexane with a fluorinated carbon attached to an ester? Wait: O[C@@]1(C(F)(F)F)CCC[C@H]1C(=C)c1ccccc1 is a cyclohexane with a fluorinated carbon bearing an O-ester linking to a carbonyl group C=C(C)C(=O). So the precursor is an ester of a keto? Actually C=C(C)C(=O)O- is an acrylate? C=C(C)C(=O)O- is isobut-2-enoate? It's an unsaturated ester. The target had a hydroxyl on the cyclohexane and a trifluoromethyl group. The precursor has an ester linking to the cyclohexane, not a hydroxyl. That matches the carbonyl-ene forward: the carbonyl-ene would convert an alkene + carbonyl to a new C-C bond and a hydroxyl. So the retro step is breaking the C-O bond (ester) to give a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene? Actually the retro template is for a carbonyl-ene: product has OH, precursor has carbonyl and alkene. So our precursor should have a carbonyl (C=O) and an alkene. Indeed we have C=C(C)C(=O)O- (an unsaturated ester) and the cyclohexane part has a C=C attached to aromatic ring (C= C c1ccccc1). So there are two alkenes? The target had a C=C at the start (exocyclic double bond) and a C=C inside the cyclohexane? Actually target: [CH2]=[C]([aryl])... The target has an exocyclic double bond attached to aromatic ring and a cyclohexane with OH. The precursor has an ester linking to cyclohexane and an exocyclic double bond on the cyclohexane? It has C= C c1ccccc1 attached to cyclohexane. That matches the target's aromatic substituent. So seems plausible.

Now we need to construct the retrosynthesis route JSON: root molecule is target SMILES, child is reaction node with template_id 1209837, children are precursor molecules (maybe just one). The apply_template returned a tuple with one SMILES. So we have one precursor.

We should verify the step is valid using verify_step.
